newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks power ahead, more gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks power ahead, more gains expected.

text.p: Croatian stocks forged ahead on Wednesday with hoteliers leading the way for the second day in a row, and traders predicted further gains in most issues this week thanks to strong customer demand.
But some said light profit taking could be on the cards for selected issues as investors reap some of recent gains.
"Who knows what will happen next week, but for this week I expect further gains," said one market participant.
Buying interest and involvement of foreign players was seen as driving stocks such as cable maker Elka and Istrian hotelier Laguna even higher, with others joining the trend.
However, traders said a higher supply of shares in chocolate maker Kras might indicate a downward slide from its current peak before too long.
Seven of 10 active issues rose, two were unchanged and one, food processor Podravka, edged down two kuna to 275 after a mixed trade.
Laguna led the gainers, leaping 350 kuna ($65) to end at a new high of 1,450 kuna. Kras, up 49 to 729 kuna, followed suit, overshooting a previous 719-kuna record set on Tuesday.
Hoteliers Istraturist, rising 40 kuna to 270 and Suncani Hvar, up 24 to 80 kuna, joined the winning streak.
Fully-listed Pliva was again not traded and its global depositary receipts (GDRs), issued at 50 to each share, headed down to $47.87/435 on the London Stock Exchange.
Another blue chip Zagrebacka Banka, the country's leading bank, was flat at 1,000 kuna. Its GDRs, representing 1/10 of each share, traded at $18.875 on Seaq International in London.
The central bank exchange rate was fixed at 5.4346 kuna to the dollar, down from 5.4551 on Tuesday. ($ = 5.403 Croatian Kuna)
